## Brand & Style

This design system captures the essence of a local Pattaya cannabis boutique, blending "Real Storefront Energy" with tropical warmth. The brand personality is grounded, helpful, and deeply relaxed, avoiding the clinical or overly "tech-focused" aesthetic of modern dispensaries.

The UI should evoke the feeling of a handmade shop sign or a printed field guide. Design elements are weighted by a "craft" quality—using physical metaphors such as ink-on-paper and warm, directional lighting to create an inviting digital garden.

## Colors

The palette is rooted in the natural flora and sunset hues of coastal Thailand.

- **Primary (Leaf Green):** Used for main actions, active states, and brand-heavy backgrounds. It represents vitality and the product itself.
- **Secondary (Warm Amber):** Inspired by golden hour lighting. Used for high-visibility highlights, star ratings, and "Speciality" tags.
- **Background (Off-white Paper):** The foundation of all views. This non-pure white reduces eye strain and mimics high-quality stationary or recycled paper.
- **Accents (Clay & Teal):** Clay is reserved for seasonal alerts or organic earth-tone badges. Teal is used sparingly for medicinal/health-focused information to differentiate from recreational content.
- **Neon Green Accent:** A specialized "Glow" state used for status indicators or online-now markers, mimicking physical shop signage.

## Typography

The typographic hierarchy relies on the contrast between an expressive, high-contrast serif and a functional, modern sans-serif.

- **Display & Headlines:** Playfair Display provides an "editorial" and premium feel. Use it for shop names, product categories, and storytelling sections. It should feel like it was typeset for a boutique menu.
- **Body & UI Elements:** Montserrat offers high legibility. Use "Regular" weight for descriptions and "Bold" for navigation or call-outs.
- **Labels:** Small labels use uppercase Montserrat with increased letter spacing to mimic stamped text on packaging.

Avoid dense clusters of information; instead, use vertical rhythm to separate "Community" stories from "Product" listings. Gutters should be wide (24px on desktop) to prevent elements from feeling cramped, echoing the relaxed Thai lifestyle.

## Brand & Style

This design system captures the essence of a local Pattaya cannabis boutique, blending "Real Storefront Energy" with tropical warmth. The brand personality is grounded, helpful, and deeply relaxed, avoiding the clinical or overly "tech-focused" aesthetic of modern dispensaries. 

The visual style is a fusion of **Tactile/Skeuomorphic** and **Minimalist** principles. It draws inspiration from natural textures like bamboo, woven rattan, and sun-bleached paper. The UI should evoke the feeling of a handmade shop sign or a printed field guide. Design elements are weighted by a "craft" quality—using physical metaphors such as ink-on-paper and warm, directional lighting to create an inviting digital garden.

## Colors

The palette is rooted in the natural flora and sunset hues of coastal Thailand.

- **Primary (Leaf Green):** Used for main actions, active states, and brand-heavy backgrounds. It represents vitality and the product itself.
- **Secondary (Warm Amber):** Inspired by golden hour lighting. Used for high-visibility highlights, star ratings, and "Speciality" tags.
- **Background (Off-white Paper):** The foundation of all views. This non-pure white reduces eye strain and mimics high-quality stationary or recycled paper.
- **Accents (Clay & Teal):** Clay is reserved for seasonal alerts or organic earth-tone badges. Teal is used sparingly for medicinal/health-focused information to differentiate from recreational content.
- **Neon Green Accent:** A specialized "Glow" state used for status indicators or online-now markers, mimicking physical shop signage.

## Typography

The typographic hierarchy relies on the contrast between an expressive, high-contrast serif and a functional, modern sans-serif.

- **Display & Headlines:** Playfair Display provides an "editorial" and premium feel. Use it for shop names, product categories, and storytelling sections. It should feel like it was typeset for a boutique menu.
- **Body & UI Elements:** Montserrat offers high legibility. Use "Regular" weight for descriptions and "Bold" for navigation or call-outs.
- **Labels:** Small labels use uppercase Montserrat with increased letter spacing to mimic stamped text on packaging.

## Layout & Spacing

The layout follows a **Fixed Grid** model for desktop to maintain the "contained" feeling of a physical storefront, while transitioning to a fluid layout on mobile.

- **Desktop:** 12-column grid with a 1200px max width.
- **Tablet:** 8-column grid with 24px margins.
- **Mobile:** 4-column grid with 16px margins.

Spacing should be generous to allow the "Off-white Paper" background to breathe. Avoid dense clusters of information; instead, use vertical rhythm to separate "Community" stories from "Product" listings.
